problems.title: Infinite off-diagonal transport cost conflicts with the intended unequal marginals
problems.source_location: Section 3.3, Eqs. (2)–(3) and Theorem 3.1, PDF p. 6.
claim: Paraphrase: Section 3.3, page 6, Eqs. (2)-(3), proposes transporting a uniform distribution over candidate nodes to a semantically biased target using a cost that is finite only on matching node indices. Theorem 3.1 and the following proof claim a unique optimal plan, convergence of Sinkhorn, and an optimal goal choice. The proof states lower semicontinuity of the cost and absolute continuity of both distributions with respect to Lebesgue measure as its hypotheses. The inspected rendered source is page 6.
analysis:
Finite cost forces \(T_{ij}=0\) whenever \(i
e j\). The row and column constraints then require both \(T_{ii}=\mu_i\) and \(T_{ii}=
u_i\), hence \(\mu=
u\). For \(\mu=(1/2,1/2)\) and \(
u=(3/4,1/4)\), every coupling must move at least \(1/4\) off diagonal, giving infinite cost. Atomic node distributions also do not meet the cited Lebesgue-absolute-continuity hypothesis.
result: The theorem does not establish a finite unique transport plan or Sinkhorn convergence for its intended unequal node marginals. This is a mathematical failure of the written planner, separate from the unmeasured experimental implementation.
repair: Equalizing the marginals restores diagonal feasibility but removes semantic redistribution. A different transport or direct goal-choice formulation would require an explicit changed objective; it is not a validated replacement for the complete navigation system.
A local correction or qualification is proposed where specified; author adoption is not established.
problems.impact_rationale: The central optimal-transport planner has no finite-cost solution for the unequal marginals it is designed to use, directly invalidating the stated existence/convergence guarantee; Major is warranted.
problems.existing_correction_status: The stated reformulations are local proposals; the June 2026 author revision retains the diagonal-cost formulation and proof. No author correction or adoption is established.

problems.title: With equal uniform marginals, the plan cannot identify the minimum-cost goal
problems.source_location: Text after Eq. (3), goal argmax, and Theorem 3.1 proof, PDF p. 6.
claim: Paraphrase: page 6 immediately after Eq. (3), the paper selects a goal by maximizing \(T_{ii}\). The proof of Theorem 3.1 then infers that this goal minimizes \(C_{ii}\) under the semantic constraint. This is the specific implication checked here.
analysis: With both marginals uniform on two nodes, the sole finite-cost coupling is \(T=I/2\), regardless of the diagonal costs. For diagonal costs \((2,1/2)\), both nodes maximize \(T_{ii}\), including the more expensive one. In general the plan is \(I/m\), so maximizing its diagonal cannot imply minimum-cost goal selection.
result: The minimum-cost goal implication is false even when finite feasibility is restored by equal uniform marginals. Merely equalizing the marginals does not repair goal selection.
repair: For direct semantic-adjusted goal cost, minimizing \(\sum_i c_ix_i\) over the simplex selects minimum-cost candidates. A distinct KL-regularized formulation with positive semantic prior \(q\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) yields \(x_i\propto q_i e^{-c_i/\varepsilon}\). These are explicit changed decision objectives with elementary optimality proofs, not empirically validated replacements for HSAN.
problems.impact_rationale: Even the finite uniform-marginal special case contradicts the main theorem's goal-optimality implication. This is a substantial failure of the planner's core mathematical guarantee and warrants Major.
problems.existing_correction_status: The stated reformulations are local proposals; the June 2026 author revision retains the diagonal-cost formulation and proof. No author correction or adoption is established.

impact_rationale: The central OT planner has no finite-cost plan for its intended unequal marginals, and its only uniform diagonal plan cannot make the claimed cost-sensitive goal choice. These directly invalidate the stated core mathematical guarantee.
